title: What is known about 1RB0RB_1RC1RA_0LD1LC_0RA1LE_1LF0LC_---1LA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RB_1RC1RA_0LD1LC_0RA1LE_1LF0LC_---1LA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves that, read in pairs, the tape at each turn is a binary word and one round trip of the head is one XOR sweep of it: find the rightmost 00, flip the letter left of it, replace every letter right of it by the XOR of itself and its right neighbour, append 11 (mstep_ok). A halt needs a 00 only at the very left end. The block of 111110 words enters the sweep only through its length mod 3 (zone_step), so Lean drops it: the machine halts from blank tape iff the zone orbit halts (halts_iff_zone), and compiled evaluation runs that orbit through the first 1.7·1015 steps without a halt. Since the arrival near step 3.3·1011 the tape holds a new zone, a stranded block of 403,835 letters with a 00 every three letters, and the old zone at the left end. Every sweep stops at the block’s first 00 or before, so by swr_append_ok the old zone cannot move, and the machine cannot halt, until the new zone has eaten the whole block. In 3·1010 sweeps from zone step 3·107 it ate about 29 letters.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: The halting pattern
claims.text: 0 0 1 C> 0, the pass on the separator right of a block of length 1 with two 0s on its left, halts three steps later (F reads 0). By the table this is the only way to halt (hand argument in the README).

claims.title: The pass
claims.text: Moving left from separator to separator, the pass cuts a block of length k+3 into k+1 and 1 and goes on (pass_split); a block of length 1 stops it (pass_stop). For all lengths and every surrounding tape.

claims.title: Crossing the block of words does not depend on its length
claims.text: The pass crosses n words 111110 in 6n steps, in the same state, turning each into 1110 10; the sweep back turns them into 111110 again. For every n and every surrounding tape.

claims.title: The macro machine
claims.text: A turn configuration RT out (D on the second cell of a pair 11 at the right end, the pairs out to its left). One macro step mstep: a left pass over the pairs (scan: skip 11; after a 01, a 11 becomes 01 and the pass goes on, a 01 becomes 11 and the head turns; at the first pair F halts), a right pass flipping every pair (apass), and at the left end either a pass in step (edgeD) or, out of step, the configuration on lists run cell by cell (rawRun) until it is a turn configuration again (asRT). mstep_sound: for all states, the machine goes where mstep says in exactly the steps it says, or halts there.

claims.title: Halting is exactly a question about the orbit
claims.text: orbT k: the k-th state of the macro machine from blank tape with its step count (orbT_sound). halts_iff: the machine halts from blank tape if and only if some macro step of the orbit halts.

claims.title: No halt in the first 4·10<sup>8</sup> steps
claims.text: The first 15,000 macro steps of the orbit, evaluated by compiled code: no halt, more than 4·10<sup>8</sup> machine steps (through the six resets of the left end).

claims.title: One round trip is one XOR sweep
claims.text: At a turn at the right end, read in pairs, the tape is a binary word. When it has a 00, one macro step is exactly one sweep: the rightmost 00 is found, the letter left of it is flipped, every letter right of it becomes the XOR of itself and its right neighbour, and 11 is appended (4d + 14 steps, d the depth of the 00). A 00 only at the very left end halts; no 00 at all is a reset at the left end.

claims.title: The leftmost-zone reduction
claims.text: For every length of the block of words the sweep does the same thing to the rest of the word; the length enters only mod 3, through one letter (zone_step). A sweep that finds its 00 early leaves everything further left untouched (swr_append_ok), and a sweep through a stretch without 00 acts beyond it only through the stretch’s last letter (swr_split).
claims.where: lean/Xor.lean (the same file for the four machines with this block)

claims.title: Halting is a question about the zone orbit
claims.text: The zone orbit keeps only the count of the block of words and the rest of the word; it uses the sweep at the right end and the pass machine at the left end. The machine halts from blank tape if and only if the zone orbit halts.

claims.title: No halt in the first 1.7·10<sup>15</sup> steps
claims.text: 3·10<sup>7</sup> steps of the zone orbit, evaluated by compiled code, without a halt; they cover more than 1.7·10<sup>15</sup> machine steps.

claims.title: No halt in 5·10<sup>11</sup> steps; the arrivals at the left end
claims.text: The real machine runs 5·1011 steps without a halt. Passes reached the left end of the tape at triggers 1, 2, 3, 6, 27, 51 (step 5,043) and 403,962 (between steps 3.25·1011 and 3.30·1011). At the last one the 134,619 words of the block stayed behind as 1110 10 and a new zone started at the right end.

claims.title: The reduced system
claims.text: With the growing block cut to 10 words at every trigger (cutting whole words keeps the length mod 3, so by zone_step the cut is exact between arrivals at the left end), the run from trigger 1,000 reaches the left end at trigger 403,962 without a halt. The real machine did the same near step 3.3·1011. Beyond that arrival the reduced run is no guide, because the block left behind is used up and its length matters.

claims.title: The leftmost zone alone
claims.text: The leftmost zone run by itself, one arriving pass at a time, from the real configuration of trigger 100, reaches the left end in tick 403,863 (trigger 403,962) with the blocks later seen in the real tape. A model, checked against the real machine at this one arrival.

claims.title: Halting needs the left end
claims.text: Every halt of the macro step happens at the left end of the word: a sweep halts exactly when the only 00 of the word is at its very left end, and the other halting cases of the pass machine are passes that run off the left end.

claims.title: Two zones
claims.text: Since the arrival near step 3.3·1011 the tape holds a new zone, a stranded block of 403,835 letters with a 00 every three letters, and the old zone at the left end. Every sweep stops at the block’s first 00 or before, so by swr_append_ok the old zone cannot move, and the machine cannot halt, until the new zone has eaten the whole block. In 3·1010 sweeps from zone step 3·107 it ate about 29 letters.
claims.where: c/xs.c, c/z1.c in the folder of 1RB0RB_1LC1RA_1LF0LD_0LE1LD_1LA1LC_---1LA, from the state written by lean/DumpState.lean; README.md

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. It halts if a pass reaches the leftmost block while that block is a lone 1 with blank tape on its left; nothing known forces or forbids that.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. A zone of about 120 cells is rewritten again and again by passes coming from the right, where a block of 111110 words keeps growing. The machine stops only if a pass gets through the whole zone and finds a lone 1 at the very left end of the tape. A pass got there near step 3.3·10<sup>11</sup>, as predicted, and did not stop the machine.

facts.text: The halting pattern: a pass meets a block of length 1 with two 0s on its left.
Crossing the block of words is proved not to depend on its length.
No halt, by compiled evaluation of the zone orbit (Lean).

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.496).
After 109 steps the tape spans 44,836 cells (21 left of the start, 32,860 right), with a density of 1s of 0.718.

sections.heading: From a tape to a small counter
html: <div class="col">

The question is whether this machine, started on a blank tape, ever halts. Nobody knows yet, but the run can be described exactly by smaller and smaller systems, each one proved in Lean to halt exactly when the one below it halts. This section is the map; each later section explains one step on it, with something to try.
<ol class="ladder">

• The tape

    Cells of 0 and 1, a head in one of six states. This is the machine itself (the simulator above).

    read in pairs at each turn at the right end Kernel

• A word

    A string of letters, one per pair of cells: 11 is 1, 01 is 0. About half as long as the tape.

    one round trip of the head = one XOR sweep Kernel

• The XOR sweep

    A four-line rule that turns one word into the next. No states, no head: just the word.

    the long block at the right end matters only through its length mod 3 Kernel

• The zone orbit

    A short word, the zone, plus one number, the length of the block. This is what Lean runs, and what your browser runs below: to 1.8·1015 machine steps in a second or two.

    a reset splits the zone in two Computed

• Two zones

    An old zone frozen at the left end, behind a stranded block, and a new zone that has to get through the block before anything can happen there.

The panel shows one moment of the real run at the first four layers at once. Pick a turn (the head coming back to the right end of the tape) and read it down: the cells, the letters those cells spell, the same letters split into zone, block and head, and the two numbers the zone orbit keeps.

sections.heading: Reading the tape as a word
html: <div class="col">

Watch the simulator for a while and one moment keeps coming back: the head arrives at the right end of the tape, in state D, with blank tape to its right. Call this a turn. At every turn the tape, read two cells at a time from the right end, is made of the pairs 11 and 01 only. So it can be written as a word: 11 is the letter 1 and 01 the letter 0. The head sits on the second cell of the last pair, which is always 11, so a word always ends in 1.

Why should anyone believe this pairing is the right way to look? Because Lean proves it. lean/Sweep.lean defines a macro step on words: the left pass (states C and its partners crossing the pairs to the left), the turn, and the right pass back, including the rare passes that run off the left end. mstep_sound proves, for every word, that the machine does exactly what the macro step says, step count included. From that, halts_iff (lean/Reduce.lean) says: the machine halts from blank tape if and only if the orbit of words from the blank tape reaches a halting macro step. From here on the tape is gone; only words are left. Kernel
An earlier check ran that orbit of words by compiled evaluation through the first 4·108 machine steps (blank_runs_orbit, lean/OrbitRun.lean). native_decide The zone orbit below goes much further.

sections.heading: One round trip is one XOR sweep
html: <div class="col">
The macro step is long, but on the words that occur at turns it does something very simple. mstep_ok (lean/Bits.lean) proves that one round trip of the head is one XOR sweep of the word: Kernel

1. find the rightmost 00 in the word;
  2. flip the letter just left of it;
  3. replace every letter right of the 00 by itself XOR its right-hand neighbour;
  4. append a 1 (the new pair 11 the head leaves at the right end).

The machine takes exactly 4·d + 14 steps for it, where d is the number of letters right of the 00. In machine terms: the left pass crosses the pairs until it finds two 01 in a row, turns there, and the way back rewrites every pair it crosses.

Two outcomes are not covered. If the only 00 is the first two letters of the word, there is nothing left of it to flip: the pass meets the left end of the tape and the machine halts (mstep_halt). If there is no 00 at all, the pass runs off the left end and the machine does something else for a while (a reset); Lean then falls back on the full macro step. So a halt needs a sweep that gets all the way to the left end of the word.
Try it. Load a turn of the real run, or type any word ending in 1, and step through the four stages. The last line runs the real machine on that word and compares.
sections.html_after: One more property drives everything below, and the XOR row shows it: a letter changes only through itself and its right neighbour. Whatever lies left of the 00 is not touched at all (swr_append_ok), and a sweep that runs through a stretch without 00 changes that stretch to its XOR differences and passes on only its last letter (swr_split, xd_append). Information moves left by at most one letter per sweep. Kernel

sections.heading: The block forgets its length
html: <div class="col">

At the right end of every word sits a long, regular stretch: …110110110, followed by the head’s 1. On the tape this is the block of words 111110 that the simulator shows growing (each letter is two cells, so 110 is 11 11 01, the six cells 111101, which is 111110 read from another starting point). It grows by one letter per sweep, and it is most of the tape: after 3·107 sweeps it has 29,596,028 letters, against a few hundred or thousand for everything else.

Every sweep crosses the whole block, because the block has no 00. Crossing it replaces each letter by its XOR with the next. For the pattern 110 repeated, the XOR differences are 011 repeated: the same pattern, moved by one place. So after a sweep the block is again a block, one letter longer, and all the zone on its left ever sees of it is one letter, the leftmost one. That letter is fixed by the length of the block mod 3.

Lean’s zone_step (lean/Xor.lean) says exactly this for every length: a sweep of «zone, block of length n + 1» is the sweep of «zone, one letter pat(n)», with the block put back in front. Kernel The panel sweeps one zone next to four blocks of consecutive lengths; the zones that come out agree whenever the lengths agree mod 3.

sections.heading: The zone orbit
html: <div class="col">

Drop the block and keep its length. What remains is the zone orbit: a state is a number n (the block’s length) and a short word Z (the zone). One step sweeps Z with the one letter pat(n) on its right and adds 1 to n; a step costs 4·(n + d) + 14 machine steps. When a sweep finds no 00 in the zone, the orbit hands that one step to the real macro step and splits the block off again afterwards.

halts_iff_zone (lean/Zone.lean) proves: the machine halts from blank tape if and only if the zone orbit halts. Kernel This is an exact reduction, not a model. And because a step of the zone orbit costs time proportional to the zone, not the tape, it can be run very far: compiled evaluation in Lean runs it for 3·107 steps, which covers the first 1.7·1015 machine steps, with no halt (zone_runs, lean/ZoneRun.lean). native_decide

The panel runs the same orbit in your browser, written separately in JavaScript. It agrees with the real machine at every turn of the first 3,000, and its state at step 3·107 (machine step 1.75·1015, block of 29,596,028 letters) is letter for letter the one Lean computes; tools/tests/test_tools.py checks both. Computed

What to look for. Most sweeps stop a few letters into the zone, next to the block: that is the left panel of the two pictures, busy in every row. Deeper sweeps are rarer and rarer, like the higher digits of a counter, which is the staircase in the depth plot. Now and then a sweep finds no 00 at all and reaches the left end of the tape; in this run that happens at zone steps 1, 2, 3, 6, 26, 50 and 403,960, none of them a halt. After the last one, at zone step 403,960 (machine step 326,299,402,270), the right-hand picture goes quiet: nothing at the left end of the tape changes again in the whole run, for a reason explained in the next section.

sections.heading: Two zones and a stranded block
html: <div class="col">

Why does the left end go quiet? At a reset the zone is rebuilt from the right end of the tape, and the letters the old zone had collected stay behind. From then on the word reads, from the left end: the old zone, a long stranded block, the new zone, the growing block and the head. The bar above the depth plot shows these parts, measured live from the orbit.

For this machine the stranded block is different from the others: it is 403,835 letters of …100100, with a 00 in every three letters. Every sweep that gets through the new zone stops at the stranded block’s first 00, so by swr_append_ok nothing left of that point can move. The new zone can only eat the stranded block from the right, a few letters at a time, and until it has eaten all of it the old zone of 63 letters is frozen and the machine cannot halt. Kernel (the lemma) Computed (that the block looks like this).

At zone step 3·107 the parts are: old zone 63 letters, stranded block 403,835, new zone 76. In 3·1010 further sweeps (run in C, c/xs.c in the folder of 1RB0RB_1LC1RA_1LF0LD_0LE1LD_1LA1LC_---1LA) the new zone ate about 29 letters. Computed

The layers below the zone orbit are all proved. The two-zone picture is not yet a proof, and nothing here decides the machine: a halt needs a sweep through the new zone, the stranded block and the old zone, all the way to the left end. Sweeps that get through the new zone came about 7 times per factor of 10 in the number of sweeps; if that goes on, the next sweep that could reach the left end is something like 101200 sweeps or more away. Heuristic Deciding the machine needs a proof about the zone orbit itself: that the new zone never lets a sweep through often enough, or that the old zone never halts whatever it is fed.

family: Counter zone beside a growing block of 111110 words; a halt needs a lone 1 at the left end of the tape
summary: A zone of about 120 cells is rewritten like a counter by passes coming from a growing block of 111110 words; a halt needs a pass that reaches a lone 1 at the left end of the tape. A pass reached the left end near step 3.3·10^11 without halting and left a reservoir of 134,619 pairs 10 1110 that shields the left end until it is used up (134,615 pairs left at step 5·10^11, where the run ends without a halt).
